To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

diatom-based transfer functions can be successfully developed for conductivity in Ugandan crater lakes and these models are more accurate when based on a regional rather than a continental training set.

1) a regional training set can be developed to improve the accuracy of conductivity reconstructions, and 2) this regional training set is more appropriate for the interpretation of the diatom record from the Lake Kasenda sediment core.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
regional training sets can be used to develop robust and reliable transfer functions, but that these should be tested against larger, more diverse, datasets to confirm their accuracy.

regional models are more appropriate than continental-scale models in the case study presented, but that regional models are not appropriate in all cases and that there are many other factors that need to be considered.
regional training sets are more appropriate for palaeo-environmental reconstruction, but that they are more labour and cost intensive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

regional training sets can be used to improve reconstructions of conductivity in western Uganda, but the EDDI training set can be used with confidence to reconstruct conductivity in the East African Rift Valley lakes.

the use of the EDDI training set for the reconstruction of conductivity in the Ugandan crater lakes is not appropriate and that a regional training set is required for accurate palaeo-environmental reconstructions.
a regional training set, developed using data from a similar lake setting, can improve palaeo-environmental interpretations compared to models developed using a more diverse training set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of regional training sets, which are more closely related to the lakes being studied, can lead to more accurate reconstructions of water chemistry, and so improved environmental inferences.

a regional training set, such as that developed here, is more appropriate for inferring past lake conditions in a given region, and should be considered as a viable alternative to the use of larger training sets, which can be more geographically distant from the study area.
the use of regional training sets is a useful approach to improving the accuracy of palynological and diatom transfer functions.
